name: levobupivacaine
notes: The pure S(-)-enantiomer of bupivacaine, developed specifically to reduce racemic bupivacaine's cardiotoxicity while keeping its local-anesthetic potency and long duration. PK is essentially that of bupivacaine; cardiotoxicity is INTERMEDIATE — less than racemic bupivacaine, more than ropivacaine (the agent-choice differentiation, v0.6 LA2). Highly bound (~97%). Concentrations in ug/mL.

protein_binding.note: ~97% bound, principally to α1-acid glycoprotein; binding saturates as for bupivacaine/ropivacaine. LA-specific free-fraction story is v0.6 LA1/LA3, distinct from the v0.5 albumin axis (binding_sensitive=false).

free_fraction_model.note: Representative capacity-limited (Langmuir, 1:1) saturable binding to α1-acid glycoprotein. Capacity ≈ AAG molar concentration (~17 µM) × levobupivacaine MW (288 g/mol, the S-enantiomer of bupivacaine) ≈ 4.9 µg/mL drug-equivalent; affinity pinned by the curated low-concentration fraction_bound (0.97). Tier-D illustrative (v0.6 LA3, §7).

cardiotoxicity_class.mechanism: S(-)-enantiomer of bupivacaine: less avid cardiac Na-channel binding and less negative inotropy than the racemate at equivalent dose, so the cardiovascular margin is wider than racemic bupivacaine's but the agent retains bupivacaine-like potency and lipophilicity (more cardiotoxic than ropivacaine).
cardiotoxicity_class.note: Bardsley 1998: at equal i.v. doses in volunteers, levobupivacaine produced smaller cardiovascular changes than rac-bupivacaine — the direct evidence for the intermediate ranking. The DIRECTION (between bupivacaine and ropivacaine) is the curated claim; the exact margin is Tier-C.
